headline: Majors hold above 200-day lines and golden crosses, but momentum has stalled while whales push coins onto exchanges at the fastest pace in three weeks.
paragraphs: The regime remains uptrend by structure: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all trade above their 200-day simple moving averages, and five of seven majors show golden crosses (the 50-day above the 200-day). Doge and ADA are the exceptions, both below their 200-day lines and without golden crosses, a split that matters only in isolation. Bitcoin is 38.8% below its 12-month high of $124,740; Ethereum sits 48.3% below $4,691. The deeper the drawdown from the high, the older the current uptrend structure appears to be, even if the price still respects the 200-day. What breaks the picture is momentum: across all seven majors, MACD is below its signal line, and RSI-14 on the large caps (BTC at 50.8, ETH at 52.6, SOL at 52.2) sits right at neutral, neither overbought nor oversold. This is a trend that has run long enough to lose acceleration but not so far that it shows exhaustion. The RSI values tell you the majors are resting, not dying.

The 24-hour action reversed most of the calendar month's gains: Bitcoin down 2.27% on the day, Ethereum down 3.52%, Solana down 3.04%. Over the last seven days, all are deeper red: Bitcoin down 4.29%, Ethereum down 2.17%, Solana down 3.66%, and Doge down 8.86%. Yet the month-to-date picture is still positive: Bitcoin up 20.37%, Ethereum up 30.54%, Solana up 35.25%. This is the core tension in the data. A market that has climbed hard in the month is now cooling on a daily and weekly basis while the longer trend structure remains intact. The volatility in realized moves is high across the board, particularly in Ethereum at 72.9% 30-day volatility and XRP at 90.9%, which speaks to larger swings in both directions. The tape is saying the uptrend has not broken, but it is not accelerating either.

Derivatives positioning shows heavy long positioning at mild funding costs. Bitcoin's long-to-short ratio on OKX sits at 1.78, meaning for every short there are nearly two longs; Ethereum's ratio is 2.16, Solana's 2.26, and Doge's 4.82. Funding rates paint the split: Bitcoin is charging longs 0.0086% per 8-hour period (9.4% annualized), which is modest and in a normal range. Ethereum's funding is near zero at negative 0.0006% per 8-hour period (negative 0.7% annualized), meaning shorts are paying longs, a rare posture that often marks consensus transition. SOL is negative 0.0043% per 8-hour (negative 4.7% annualized), also favoring longs. Open interest remains substantial across majors: Bitcoin at $2.22 billion, Ethereum at $1.57 billion, Solana at $264 million. In the last hour, liquidations were small and almost entirely on the short side for BTC and ETH (ETH: $394k shorts liquidated, zero longs), but SOL saw longs getting cleaned at $1.21 million versus $8.9k on shorts. The positioning is not dangerously crowded at current funding costs, but the directional bias (long-heavy across the board) means any sharp move lower would hurt the majority of leveraged accounts.

Whale flows broke decisively onto exchanges in the last 24 hours: $174.2 million net moved onto trading venues, led by Ethereum at $126 million and Bitcoin at $76.9 million (with ETH split between two Coinbase institutional wallets and BTC going to Binance). This is the largest daily on-exchange move in three weeks; the week ending September 15 alone saw $739 million move onto exchanges, versus $225 million the week prior and $49 million in early September. That four-week pattern, combined with today's large single-day push, suggests either liquidation pressure, whale profit-taking, or preparation for a large market move. The stablecoin float sits at $310.3 billion, up only 1.35% on the month, which means while coins are moving onto exchanges, the dry powder available to buy into any weakness has not expanded. This is a crucial asymmetry: supply is arriving at the venue, but demand capital is flat.

Spot ETF flows offer a split read that requires careful naming: over the last 24 hours, Bitcoin ETFs saw an inflow of $159.9 million on September 14, but over the last five sessions, the net was an outflow of $302.8 million. For Ethereum, the picture is aligned: an inflow of $121.1 million on September 14 and an inflow of $318.0 million over five sessions. BTC's window disagreement matters; the daily inflow is offset by earlier outflows, suggesting institutional interest in dips is present but intermittent. ETH's two-directional agreement (both windows inflow) suggests steadier institutional accumulation. Total market cap fell 4.77% in the 24 hours, and Bitcoin dominance at 58.3% is holding firm.

The Fear & Greed gauge reads 69 (Greed), sitting near the top of its 30-day range of 31 to 74, which is consistent with a month that has rallied hard on the calendar. Small-cap movers show rotation: gainers like FF (up 12.13%), PONS (11.15%), and ARB (9.67%) versus losers like FIL (down 11.61%), INJ (down 8.17%), and ZRO (down 8.14%). Bitcoin network difficulty is rising 5.1%, indicating sustained hash rate confidence. Watch for a reversal in whale on-exchange flows; sustained inflows at this pace paired with flat stablecoin float would flag either capitulation selling or a pending large transfer. A break below the 200-day line on the majors, particularly if accompanied by a MACD cross below signal, would mark the end of the current uptrend structure. Until either of those conditions appears, the tape shows a rested uptrend vulnerable to short-term pullback but not broken.
